mainTopic: How long חמץ was forbidden in Egypt compared with later generations, and when the תמורה of a lost קרבן פסח is offered as a שלמים
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining the previous משנה. It concludes that the קרבן פסח is eaten on one night, both in Egypt and in later generations. The difference is חמץ: it was forbidden for one day in Egypt and is forbidden for seven days in later generations. A new משנה follows. רבי יהושע heard two opposite rulings about the תמורה of a קרבן פסח, and רבי עקיבא explains them. If a lost פסח is found before the replacement is slaughtered, the animal and its תמורה graze until they get a מום, and their money buys a שלמים. If it is found after the slaughter, the animal and its תמורה are offered as שלמים. רבה and רבי זירא disagree whether the cutoff is the slaughter itself or חצות, and the גמרא shows the same disagreement among תנאים. רבא then rules on an animal found before the slaughter but exchanged after it. אביי challenges him from the ברייתא on ״אם כשב״, and the גמרא answers that the פסוק is only an אסמכתא and explains its true lessons. In a second version, רבא rules the opposite way about that same case, and אביי's challenge to that version continues on the next amud.

steps.title: 'All seven days' refers to the חמץ prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'פסח דורות applies all seven days' cannot mean eating the קרבן, so it must mean the prohibition of חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering its earlier question about the משנה. It explains that 'all seven days' refers to the prohibition of חמץ, not to eating the קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן פסח is eaten only on one night, both in Egypt and in later generations. So the 'seven days' in the משנה cannot describe eating the קרבן. It must describe how long חמץ is forbidden in later generations.

keyTerms.meaning: Leavened food, forbidden on פסח
The פסח of later generations, after the Exodus
Rather (introduces a corrected explanation)

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to leavened bread.
phrases.notes: This continues a question on the previous amud: what does 'applies all seven days' refer to?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the גמרא's question on the previous amud about what 'all seven days' in the משנה refers to.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seven days in the משנה refer to the prohibition of חמץ in פסח דורות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'נוהג כל שבעה' in the משנה refer to?

steps.title: Was חמץ forbidden for only one night in Egypt?
steps.stepSummary: If 'seven days' means חמץ in later generations, then the matching phrase 'one night' would seem to mean that חמץ in Egypt was forbidden for just one night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this imply that in פסח מצרים, חמץ was forbidden for one night and no more?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the last answer and questions it. If 'seven days' is about חמץ, then 'one night' should also be about חמץ, which suggests חמץ was forbidden in Egypt for only one night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה contrasts 'one night' (Egypt) with 'seven days' (later generations). If the second half is about חמץ, the first half seems to be about חמץ too. That would mean the חמץ prohibition in Egypt ended after one night. This step sets up the challenge that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication, from the inference
The פסח kept in Egypt at the Exodus
And no more

phrases.english: By inference, that the Passover of Egypt
phrases.notes: מכלל means 'it follows from': we're drawing a conclusion from what was just said.

phrases.english: was one night and no more?
phrases.notes: Asked in surprise. It leads straight into a challenge.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּפֶסַח מִצְרַיִם לַיְלָה אֶחָד וְתוּ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a problematic implication from the answer in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the משנה in step 1, where 'one night' and 'seven days' both refer to חמץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two halves of the contrast are parallel, then חמץ in Egypt was forbidden for only one night, which seems wrong.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: חמץ in Egypt was forbidden for a full day
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches from the closeness of two פסוקים that חמץ in Egypt was forbidden for one day. That means a night and a day, not just one night.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא that רבי יוסי הגלילי says: From where do we know that the חמץ prohibition of פסח מצרים applied for only one day? The פסוק says, 'No חמץ shall be eaten,' and right next to it, 'Today you are going out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that the inference in step 2 is wrong. In Egypt, חמץ was forbidden for a whole day, not only one night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from two neighboring פסוקים: 'לא יאכל חמץ' is placed next to 'היום אתם יוצאים.' So the חמץ prohibition in Egypt lasted 'one day,' which includes daytime. This clashes with a reading of the משנה that limits it to one night.

keyTerms.meaning: Its prohibition of חמץ
The פסוק teaches
Placed right next to it (a סמוכים derivation)

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
From where do we know regarding the Passover of Egypt

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין חִימּוּצוֹ נוֹהֵג אֶלָּא יוֹם אֶחָד —
phrases.english: that its leaven prohibition applied for only one day?
The verse states: "No leavened bread shall be eaten"
phrases.notes: שמות יג:ג

phrases.english: and right next to it: "Today you are going out."
phrases.notes: שמות יג:ד. Because these פסוקים sit right next to each other, the חמץ rule gets tied to 'one day.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that gives the challenge in step 2 its force.
steps.raayaObject: That חמץ in פסח מצרים was forbidden for more than just one night
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יוסי הגלילי, learned from the closeness of 'לא יאכל חמץ' to 'היום אתם יוצאים'
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'one night' in the משנה describes the חמץ prohibition in Egypt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows that the Egyptian חמץ prohibition lasted a full day, not one night.

steps.title: Rereading the משנה: 'one night' is about eating, and חמץ lasted all day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the משנה differently. 'One night' refers to eating the קרבן, which is the same in every generation. The חמץ prohibition lasted one full day in Egypt and lasts seven days in later generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what the משנה means: the קרבן is eaten on one night, and the same is true for פסח דורות. Its חמץ prohibition applied the whole day in Egypt, while in פסח דורות it applies all seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the משנה in a new way. 'One night' is about eating the קרבן, and the difference between Egypt and later generations is only about how long חמץ is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two halves of the משנה are no longer read as a simple parallel. Eating the קרבן on one night is the same for both. The real difference is חמץ: one day in Egypt, matching רבי יוסי הגלילי, and seven days in later generations.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a rereading of the source)
And the same applies
All seven days

steps.whatToRemember: פסח מצרים and פסח דורות are the same for eating the קרבן: one night. They differ on חמץ: one day in Egypt, seven days in later generations.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the קרבן פסח in later generations is eaten for seven days. The 'seven days' is only about the חמץ prohibition. The קרבן itself is always eaten on one night.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: לַיְלָה אֶחָד, וְהוּא הַדִּין לְפֶסַח דּוֹרוֹת.
phrases.english: It is eaten on one night, and the same is true for the Passover of later generations.
And its leaven prohibition in Egypt lasted the entire day,
while the Passover of later generations applies all seven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge from the ברייתא by rereading the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה (הכי קאמר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'One night' and 'seven days' were both about חמץ, which would mean חמץ in Egypt lasted one night.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'One night' is about eating the קרבן, the same in all generations. חמץ lasted one day in Egypt and seven days in later generations.

steps.title: רבי יהושע heard two opposite rulings about תמורת פסח
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. רבי יהושע received two traditions: one says the תמורה of a פסח is offered, and the other says it is not offered. He cannot explain when each one applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי יהושע said: I heard that the תמורה of a פסח is offered, and that the תמורה of a פסח is not offered, and I cannot explain it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins on a new topic. רבי יהושע reports two traditions that seem to contradict each other about the תמורה of a קרבן פסח, and he admits he does not know how they fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תמורה is an animal someone tries to swap for a קרבן. It also becomes holy and does not replace the original. רבי יהושע knows both rulings but has forgotten which case each one belongs to. This sets up רבי עקיבא's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
An animal one tries to substitute for a קרבן. It becomes holy too.
Is offered on the מזבח (here, as a שלמים)
I heard (from my teachers)
To explain

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Rabbi Yehoshua said: I heard
that the substitute of a Paschal lamb is offered,
phrases.notes: It is offered as a שלמים, since a תמורה cannot itself be a קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: and that the substitute of a Paschal lamb is not offered,
and I cannot explain it.
phrases.notes: He does not remember which case each ruling applies to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, separate from the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two traditions: in some case the תמורת פסח is offered, and in another it is not.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא explains: a lost פסח found before the slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא gives the first case. A פסח was lost and replaced, then found before the replacement was slaughtered. It must graze until it gets a מום, be sold, and the money is used for a שלמים. The same is true of its תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: I will explain. A פסח that is found before the slaughter of the פסח must graze until it becomes blemished. Then it is sold, and the owner brings a שלמים with the money. The same applies to its תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא begins to explain רבי יהושע's two traditions. He describes the case where the פסח itself, and also its תמורה, are not offered at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner lost his פסח and set aside another one. The first animal turned up while it was still time to slaughter the פסח. Because it was set aside (נדחה) at the time of the slaughter, it cannot be offered. It waits until it has a מום, is sold, and the money buys a שלמים. Its תמורה has the same fate, so this is the case of 'the תמורה is not offered.'

keyTerms.meaning: The slaughter of the קרבן פסח (here, of the replacement animal)
It must graze (be left in the pasture)
Until it becomes blemished and unfit
With its money (the sale proceeds)
A peace-offering

steps.confusionAlert: Here the תמורה is NOT offered itself. It grazes like the original animal. Only the money from selling it buys a שלמים. The case where a תמורה is offered comes next in the משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first half of a classic rule: whether a leftover פסח can become a שלמים depends on whether it was available, and so rejected, at the time of the slaughter.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said: I will explain:
A Paschal lamb that was lost and then found
phrases.notes: The owner had already set aside a replacement.

phrases.english: before the slaughter of the Paschal lamb —
must graze until it becomes blemished,
and it is sold, and he brings a peace-offering with its money.
And the same applies to its substitute.
phrases.notes: This is the case where 'תמורת פסח אינה קריבה.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering רבי יהושע's puzzle by giving the case of 'not offered.'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the lost פסח is found before the slaughter, it and its תמורה graze until blemished. They are sold, and the money buys a שלמים, so the תמורה is not offered.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When is the תמורת פסח not offered, and when is it offered?

steps.title: Second case: the lost animal is found after the slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא finishes his answer. If the lost פסח is found after the replacement was slaughtered, it is offered as a שלמים, and so is its תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if it was found after the slaughter of the פסח, it is offered as a שלמים. The same is true of its תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives the second half of his answer. This is the case where the תמורה of a פסח IS offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, the animal was found before the replacement was slaughtered, so it could not be offered and had to graze. Here it was found only after the slaughter, so it can go straight onto the מזבח as a שלמים. Its תמורה follows the same rule. This explains the tradition that 'the תמורה of a פסח is offered.'

keyTerms.meaning: Peace-offering. A leftover פסח becomes this kind of קרבן.
An animal someone tried to 'swap' in place of a holy animal. It becomes holy too.
And the same is true

steps.whatToRemember: Found BEFORE the slaughter: it grazes until it gets a מום, then the money buys a שלמים. Found AFTER the slaughter: it is offered right away as a שלמים. In each case, the תמורה follows the same rule.

phrases.english: After the slaughter of the Paschal lamb (the replacement),
it is offered as a peace-offering.
And so too its substitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי עקיבא's two-part answer that began in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The tradition 'the תמורה of a פסח is offered' refers to a lost פסח that was found after the replacement was slaughtered.

steps.title: Why mention the תמורה at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the animal and its תמורה follow the same rule, why didn't רבי יהושע just say 'a פסח is offered' and 'a פסח is not offered'?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Let him say: 'A פסח is offered, and a פסח is not offered.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks about the wording of רבי יהושע's traditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי עקיבא's explanation, the תמורה always follows the original animal. So the traditions could have been stated about the פסח itself. Bringing in the תמורה looks like extra words.

keyTerms.meaning: So let him say (a challenge to the wording)
Is offered on the מזבח
Is not offered

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Let him say: The Paschal lamb is offered,
and the Paschal lamb is not offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא: פֶּסַח קָרֵב וּפֶסַח אֵינוֹ קָרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the משנה's wording now that רבי עקיבא's explanation is complete.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'the תמורה of a פסח' in רבי יהושע's two traditions.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תמורה always follows the original animal, so speaking about the תמורה seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The wording teaches that some תמורה is never offered
steps.stepSummary: The wording teaches that there is a case where the תמורה of a פסח is not offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that there is a תמורה of a פסח that is not offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question in step 8. Mentioning the תמורה teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought that a תמורה of a פסח always becomes a שלמים, because it can never be a פסח itself. The wording teaches that this is wrong. If the original animal cannot be offered, its תמורה cannot be offered either.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
That there is (a case)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think every תמורה of a פסח automatically goes on the מזבח as a שלמים. If the original animal has to graze, the תמורה has to graze too.

phrases.english: This teaches us
that there is a substitute of a Paschal lamb
that is not offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra words come to teach something new.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A תמורה of a פסח is always offered as a שלמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Some תמורה of a פסח is not offered, namely when the original animal itself cannot be offered.

steps.title: רבה and רבי זירא disagree about the cutoff
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the cutoff is the actual slaughter of the replacement. רבי זירא says the cutoff is midday (חצות).
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבה said, we learned 'before the slaughter and after the slaughter.' רבי זירא said, we learned 'before midday and after midday.'
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים disagree about the point that separates רבי עקיבא's two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבה, what matters is when the replacement animal is actually slaughtered. For רבי זירא, what matters is חצות, the time when the פסח may first be slaughtered. So if the animal is found after midday but before the slaughter, רבי זירא treats it as found 'after,' and it is offered as a שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Midday, the time when slaughtering the פסח may begin
Before

steps.whyThisMatters: The two opinions give different results for an animal found between midday and the slaughter of the replacement.

phrases.english: It was stated: Rabba said:
We learned 'before the slaughter and after the slaughter.'
Rabbi Zeira said:
We learned 'before midday and after midday.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to defining the cutoff point in רבי עקיבא's cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה: the cutoff is the actual slaughter. רבי זירא: the cutoff is חצות.

steps.title: The משנה says 'slaughter,' not 'midday'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא: the משנה clearly says 'before the slaughter of the פסח.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי זירא, doesn't the משנה say 'before the slaughter of the פסח'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי זירא's opinion using the plain words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks about the slaughter, which fits רבה. רבי זירא's 'midday' does not seem to match the text.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches (explicitly)

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Zeira,
doesn't it teach 'before the slaughter of the Paschal lamb'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's side of the dispute in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's view that the cutoff is חצות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly says 'slaughter,' which seems to support רבה.

steps.title: Read it as 'before the time of slaughter'
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא reads the משנה as 'before the time of the slaughter of the פסח,' which is חצות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: 'before the time of the slaughter of the פסח.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי זירא by reading the משנה's words a little differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Slaughter' here means the time when slaughtering may begin, not the actual act. That time is חצות, so the משנה fits רבי זירא after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read the text this way)
Time

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי זירא, 'before the slaughter' in the משנה means before חצות, the time when slaughtering may begin. For רבה, it means before the actual slaughter.

phrases.english: Say:
'before the time of the slaughter of the Paschal lamb.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to רבי זירא in step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Slaughter' means the actual act of slaughtering.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Slaughter' means the time when slaughtering may begin, which is חצות.

steps.title: The argument between the אמוראים matches an argument between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the argument between רבה and רבי זירא is the same as an older argument between the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like an argument between תנאים. A פסח that was lost and then found before the slaughter must graze. If it was found after the slaughter, it is offered. רבי אליעזר says: if found before חצות, it must graze. If found after חצות, it is offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the argument we just learned between רבה and רבי זירא was already argued by earlier sages, the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says the cutoff is the actual slaughter of the replacement animal. That is just like רבה. רבי אליעזר says the cutoff is חצות, which is just like רבי זירא. This shows that neither אמורא invented a new idea; each one follows a תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like an argument among the תנאים (the sages of the משנה era)
It must graze. The animal is left in the pasture until it gets a blemish, and then it is sold.
It is offered on the מזבח (here, as a שלמים)
Midday, when the time for slaughtering the פסח begins

steps.confusionAlert: The animal being discussed here is the ORIGINAL פסח that was lost and later found. The 'slaughter' mentioned is the slaughter of the REPLACEMENT animal that was set aside in its place.

phrases.english: This is like a dispute of Tannaim.
phrases.notes: The argument between רבה and רבי זירא matches an older one.

phrases.english: A Pesach that was found before the slaughter must graze,
phrases.notes: Before the replacement was slaughtered. This matches רבה.

phrases.english: after the slaughter, it is offered.
phrases.notes: It is offered as a שלמים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
before midday, it must graze,
phrases.notes: This matches רבי זירא.

phrases.english: after midday, it is offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the רבה/רבי זירא argument by tying each side to a תנא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא matches רבה (the cutoff is the slaughter itself). רבי אליעזר matches רבי זירא (the cutoff is חצות).
steps.whatToRemember: רבה = the cutoff is the actual slaughter (the תנא קמא). רבי זירא = the cutoff is חצות (רבי אליעזר).

steps.title: רבא limits when the substitute may be offered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling about bringing a שלמים after the slaughter. רבא says this applies only when the animal was both found AND exchanged after the slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'After the slaughter of the פסח, he brings a שלמים, etc.' רבא said: This was taught only when the animal was found after the slaughter and he exchanged it after the slaughter. But if it was found before the slaughter and he exchanged it after the slaughter, its תמורה comes from the power of pushed-off holiness, so it is not offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה. רבא then explains that this line covers only one specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the original animal was found before the slaughter, it was already 'pushed off' from being offered, and it must graze. A תמורה gets its holiness from the original animal. So if the original was pushed off, the תמורה is pushed off too, even though the exchange happened later.

keyTerms.meaning: A substitute animal. Someone tries to swap a non-holy animal for a holy one, and both become holy.
He made the exchange (performed תמורה)
Pushed-off holiness: holiness that has been rejected from being offered
They only taught this in the case of… (a formula that limits a ruling)

steps.confusionAlert: This is רבא, not רבה from step 10. They are two different אמוראים.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up a key principle: a תמורה takes on the status of its source animal at the moment that animal was found, not at the moment the exchange was made.

phrases.aramaic: אַחַר שְׁחִיטַת הַפֶּסַח יָבִיא שְׁלָמִים וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: 'After the slaughter of the Pesach, he brings a peace-offering, etc.'
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּמְצָא אַחַר שְׁחִיטָה
phrases.english: They taught this only when it was found after the slaughter
and he exchanged it after the slaughter.
But if it was found before the slaughter
and he exchanged it after the slaughter —

phrases.aramaic: תְּמוּרָתוֹ מִכֹּחַ קְדוּשָּׁה דְּחוּיָה קָא אָתָא,
phrases.english: its substitute comes from the power of pushed-off holiness,
phrases.notes: The original animal was already pushed off once it was found before the slaughter.

phrases.english: and it is not offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תמורה may be offered as a שלמים only if the original was found after the slaughter. If the original was found before the slaughter, the תמורה is pushed off, even if the exchange was made after the slaughter.

steps.title: אביי cites a ברייתא that includes the תמורה as a שלמים
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא that reads 'אם כשב' as including the תמורה of a פסח, after the פסח, as a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him: The verse says 'If a lamb.' Why does the verse need to say 'If a lamb'? To include the תמורה of a פסח, after the פסח, that it is offered as a שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins a challenge to רבא by quoting a ברייתא. This step only sets up the source; the actual attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from the extra words 'אם כשב' that a פסח's תמורה, after the פסח time, can be a שלמים. It gives no details about when the animal was found. אביי will argue next that it must mean the case רבא forbade.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the verse need to say this? (it seems extra)
To include
'If a lamb' (ויקרא ג:ז), in the section on שלמים

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
'If a lamb': why does the verse state 'If a lamb'?
To include the substitute of a Pesach after the Pesach
that it is offered as a peace-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a challenge against רבא's limit.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the תמורה of a פסח found before the slaughter is not offered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse explicitly includes the תמורה of a פסח as a שלמים. The next step shows this must refer to רבא's forbidden case.

steps.title: The verse must be teaching the case רבא forbade
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the verse cannot be needed for the obvious case. So it must permit an animal found before the slaughter and exchanged after it, which goes against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say it was found after the slaughter and exchanged after the slaughter, that is obvious! Why would I need a verse? Rather, isn't it that it was found before the slaughter and exchanged after the slaughter?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי completes his challenge. He shows that the ברייתא must be talking about exactly the case where רבא said the תמורה is NOT offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the original animal was found after the slaughter, it is itself a full שלמים, so of course its תמורה is a שלמים too. No verse is needed for that. A verse must teach something new, so it must permit the תמורה even when the original was found before the slaughter, and that directly contradicts רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?
If you say…
It is obvious!
Rather, is it not…? (pushing toward the only remaining option)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's argument: a verse is never wasted on the obvious. So 'אם כשב' must permit the תמורה even when the original was found before the slaughter, against רבא.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say it was found after the slaughter
and he exchanged it after the slaughter —
it is obvious! Why do I need a verse?
phrases.notes: The original animal is already a full שלמים.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that it was found before the slaughter
and he exchanged it after the slaughter!
phrases.notes: This is exactly the case רבא forbade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge that began in step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rule out the obvious case. The only case left for the verse is the one רבא forbade, so the verse permits what רבא prohibited.

steps.title: The verse is only a supporting hint
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers אביי. The case really is the obvious one: the animal was found after the slaughter and exchanged after the slaughter. The verse is only an אסמכתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, it is a case where the animal was found after the slaughter and he exchanged it after the slaughter. The verse is just a supporting hint.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא against אביי's challenge from Step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי argued that a verse would not be needed for an obvious case. The answer agrees that this case is obvious. It says the verse is not the real source at all, only an אסמכתא, so it proves nothing against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (I stick to my original reading)
Merely a supporting hint from a verse, not the true source
He exchanged (made a substitute animal)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is admitting a verse is needed here. It is saying the opposite: the law is obvious, and the verse is only a hint attached to it.

phrases.english: No, really it is where it was found after the slaughter
and he exchanged it after the slaughter,
and the verse is merely a supporting hint.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from Step 16 and defends רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the verse as an אסמכתא rather than a true derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse must teach something new, so it must permit an animal found before the slaughter, which goes against רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse is only an אסמכתא for an obvious case. רבא's limitation still stands.

steps.title: Then what is the verse for?
steps.stepSummary: If the verse is only a hint, the גמרא asks what it really comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what does the verse come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. It is setting up the next move, where it will show the real purpose of the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק in the תורה should teach something. Since the פסוק is no longer the source for the obvious case, the גמרא must find its true lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: For what purpose does it come?
The verse

phrases.english: But the verse, for what does it come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from calling the verse an אסמכתא in Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The true teaching of the verse ״כשב״ / ״אם כשב״.

steps.title: The word lamb includes the פסח for the fat tail
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. ״כשב״ includes the פסח in the rule that the אליה is burned on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: ״כשב״ comes to include the פסח for the fat tail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by quoting a ברייתא that gives the verse real lessons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים about the פסח never say its אליה goes on the מזבח. The word ״כשב״ in the laws of שלמים teaches that the פסח follows this rule too.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
The fat tail of a sheep, burned on the מזבח
To include

phrases.english: As it was taught: "Lamb"
comes to include the Paschal lamb for the fat tail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״כשב״ teaches that the פסח's אליה is burned on the מזבח.

steps.title: Leftover פסח animals are full שלמים
steps.stepSummary: ״אם כשב״ includes a פסח whose year has passed and שלמים that come because of a פסח in all the laws of שלמים: סמיכה, נסכים, and waving the חזה ושוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says ״אם כשב״, it comes to include a פסח whose year has passed, and שלמים that come because of a פסח, in all the laws of שלמים. They need leaning, libations, and the waving of the breast and thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and gives the main real lesson of ״אם כשב״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״אם כשב״ teaches that these animals are treated exactly like regular שלמים. So the verse's true job is to teach which שלמים laws apply to them, not when a substitute is allowed. That is why it can serve only as a hint for the obvious case (found after the slaughter and exchanged after it).

keyTerms.meaning: A פסח animal older than one year, too old to be a פסח
Peace-offerings that come because of a פסח
Leaning one's hands on the animal
Libations (wine, flour, and oil)
Waving the breast and thigh

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a leftover פסח becomes a complete שלמים with every one of its laws. It is not a partial or special category.

phrases.english: When it says "If a lamb,"
it comes to include a Paschal lamb whose year has passed,
and peace-offerings that come because of a Paschal lamb,
for all the מצוות of peace-offerings,
so that it requires leaning and libations
and waving of the breast and thigh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from Step 19 with the second derivation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״אם כשב״ teaches that a leftover or over-age פסח is a full שלמים in every law.

steps.title: A goat does not need its fat tail burned
steps.stepSummary: ״ואם עז״ starts a new topic. It teaches that a goat offering does not need its אליה burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when it says ״ואם עז״, it broke off the topic. This teaches that a goat does not require the fat tail.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by explaining the next phrase, about a goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ״ואם עז״ separate the goat from the lamb section. So the lamb's rule of burning the אליה does not carry over to a goat.

keyTerms.meaning: It interrupted the topic (started a new section)
Goat

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule stands. The verse is only an אסמכתא for the obvious case. Its true lessons are: the פסח needs its אליה burned; a leftover פסח is a full שלמים; and a goat has no אליה requirement.

phrases.english: And when it says "And if a goat" —
it interrupted the matter,

phrases.aramaic: לִימֵּד עַל הָעֵז שֶׁאֵין טְעוּנָה אַלְיָה.
phrases.english: teaching about the goat that it does not require the fat tail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A goat offering does not require its אליה to be burned, because ״ואם עז״ separates it from the lamb section.

steps.title: A second version: the dispute is placed on the first clause of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says some people teach the רבא–אביי argument on the רישא of the משנה, and quotes that clause: a פסח found before the slaughter must graze until blemished, be sold, and its money used for שלמים, and the same applies to its תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this argument on the first part of the משנה: A פסח that was found before the slaughter of the replacement פסח must graze until it gets a blemish, then be sold, and with its money he brings שלמים. The same is true of its substitute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is opening a second version of the argument it just finished. This line is a setup: it quotes the part of the משנה that רבא will comment on next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רבא's comment was attached to the סיפא (found after the slaughter). In this version it is attached to the רישא (found before the slaughter), where the משנה says the animal and its תמורה must graze until blemished and only their money buys שלמים. Both versions debate the same in-between case: found before the slaughter, but exchanged after it.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach it (this argument) in a different way
The first clause of the משנה
It grazes until it gets a blemish (and becomes unfit)
With its money (the money from selling it)
A substitute animal; someone tried to swap a regular animal for a קרבן, and both become holy

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two versions. Both discuss an animal found before the slaughter and exchanged after it, but they reach opposite results. In the first version (step 14), רבא says that תמורה is NOT offered. In this version (step 23), רבא says it IS offered as שלמים.

phrases.english: Some teach it on the first clause:
A Paschal lamb that was found before the slaughter of the (replacement) Paschal lamb —
must graze until it becomes blemished, and be sold,
phrases.notes: It cannot be offered as is, so it must first become unfit.

phrases.english: and he brings a peace-offering with its money.
And the same is true of its substitute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the רבא–אביי argument, now attached to the רישא instead of the סיפא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסח found before the slaughter, and its תמורה, graze until blemished. Their money buys שלמים.

steps.title: רבא limits the משנה: an exchange made after the slaughter is offered as שלמים
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה only speaks when the animal was found and exchanged before the slaughter. If it was found before but exchanged after the slaughter, the תמורה itself is offered as שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The משנה only taught this when the animal was found before the slaughter and he made the exchange before the slaughter. But if it was found before the slaughter and he made the exchange after the slaughter, its substitute is offered as שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא narrows the משנה's rule. The ״graze until blemished״ rule for the תמורה applies only if the exchange happened before the slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two moments matter: when the original was found and when the exchange was made. רבא says that even if the original was found before the slaughter, an exchange made afterward produces a תמורה that is offered directly as שלמים. It does not need to graze.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of… (a limiting formula)
He made an exchange with it (created a תמורה)
It is offered as a peace-offering

phrases.english: Rava said: They taught this only
where it was found before the slaughter
and he made the exchange before the slaughter,
but if it was found before the slaughter
and he made the exchange after the slaughter —
its substitute is offered as a peace-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא comments on and limits the רישא just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the original was found before the slaughter but the exchange was made after it, the תמורה is offered as שלמים.

steps.title: What is רבא's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the timing of the exchange should change the outcome.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the logic behind רבא's rule. This short question sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original animal was found before the slaughter, so it is pushed off. One would expect its תמורה to share that status. The גמרא wants to know why it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבא's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why an exchange made after the slaughter produces a תמורה offered as שלמים, even though the original was found before.

steps.title: The slaughter only fixes the status of an animal that could be a פסח
steps.stepSummary: The slaughter of the replacement פסח only fixes the status of animals that were already sanctified and standing for a פסח at that moment. A תמורה made after the slaughter was not yet holy then, so the slaughter does not fix its status.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the slaughter fixes the status only of something that is fit for it. Something that is not fit for it, the slaughter does not fix.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבא's logic. The slaughter's power to lock in a status only works on an animal that could itself have been brought as a פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Found before the slaughter means the original פסח was pushed aside at the moment of slaughter, and that locks its status. A תמורה made after the slaughter was not yet holy at that moment, so nothing was locked onto it, and it simply goes to שלמים. A תמורה made before the slaughter, though, is locked and pushed aside together with its source.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixes, establishes (a status)
Fit, eligible

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle explains רבא's whole position: the slaughter locks only what was already sanctified when it happened, so timing decides everything.

phrases.english: The slaughter establishes (a status)
only for something that is fit for it.

phrases.aramaic: מִידֵּי דְּלָא חֲזֵי לֵיהּ — לָא קָבְעָה.
phrases.english: Something that is not fit for it, it does not establish.
phrases.notes: Here 'not fit' means a תמורה made after the slaughter, which was not yet sanctified at that moment, so nothing was locked onto it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָבְעָה שְׁחִיטָה מִידֵּי דַּחֲזֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מאי טעמא question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The slaughter only fixes the status of an animal fit to be a פסח. A תמורה made after the slaughter was not yet sanctified at that moment, so nothing was locked onto it.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבא from the ברייתא on ״אם כשב״
steps.stepSummary: In this second version, אביי again challenges רבא from the same ברייתא: ״אם כשב״ includes the תמורה of a פסח, after the פסח, as a שלמים. How the ברייתא contradicts רבא is spelled out on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: Why does the verse say ״אם כשב״? To include the substitute of a פסח after the פסח, that it is offered as שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: In the second version, אביי attacks רבא's ruling using the same ברייתא the גמרא quoted earlier. The amud ends here. The rest of his argument and the answer come on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection uses the same ברייתא as the first version, but רבא's position is different now. Here רבא says an exchange made after the slaughter is offered as שלמים even when the original was found before. Exactly how אביי uses the ברייתא against this view is spelled out on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the verse need to say this?
To include

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
"If a lamb": why does the verse say this?
To include the substitute of a Paschal lamb
after Passover, that it is offered as a peace-offering.
phrases.notes: The objection continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling and reasoning from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that a תמורה made after the slaughter is offered as שלמים even when the original was found before the slaughter.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי cites a ברייתא that includes the תמורה of a פסח, after the פסח, as a שלמים. The exact contradiction with רבא is developed on the next amud.
